output.brief:
The cancellations are mainly a Quillbook problem, not a price problem. Quillbook's v2 invoice interface was retired on 30 March. Since then the connector has sometimes reported success without writing invoices, and retries sometimes create duplicates. Among Quillbook-connected accounts, 34% of those with recorded failures had cancelled, against 8% of those without. Churn in repriced accounts with no connector stayed flat (1.8% to 1.9%), and Founders accounts on Quillbook rose even though their price did not change. That points away from price. Tallymarsh changes are small and its logs are unreviewed, so that is unresolved. I am fairly confident about the Quillbook link. I am less sure about how much of the rise is due to support delays, which I have not tested.

Next steps: (1) Make the Quillbook fix a top priority now. The v3 move is currently rated Sev-3 and unscheduled, so it needs a date and owner. Contact affected accounts to correct their invoices. (2) Do not switch off the duplicate-invoice hold; it is stopping duplicates from reaching customers' books. (3) Do not roll back the price rise or rebuild Tallymarsh yet. (4) Review the Tallymarsh logs and monitor support response times.
